title: "Collection of samples for the development and validation of analytical methods in Clinical Pharmacology (KPE37)"
summary: The identification and quantification of chemical substances in blood, other body fluids as well as different tissue types by various analytical methods including mass spectrometry are routine workflows in modern patient care and medical research. In the research field of Clinical Pharmacology, one of the scientific aims is the development and validation of such analytical methods. This can involve either the development of new methods targeting the detection and quantification of formerly unknown substances, or the application of already established methods for known compounds to a new sample material. Thus, for example, formerly unknown metabolites of drugs can be measured or new biomarkers for special diseases can be defined which both may help to improve direct patient care in the longterm. Since additionally present substances can often have a strong impact on the analytical measurement results, it is of utmost importance to investigate the validity of the developed methods on real samples. This involves the investigation of samples collected from different persons as well as the investigation of samples used to determine whether the new methods are able to detect the respective substance accurately in repeated measurements or after a long storage time. Therefore, we require blood, saliva and urine samples which we would like to collect in a larger number and in a standardized way as outlined in the present study.
conditions: endogenous biomarkers and different types of metabolites

interventions.name: Blood samples, saliva samples and urine samples of the participants are collected. Afterwards, these samples should be used as references for the development of new analytical methods in Clinical Pharmacology.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
medical contraindication against the planned type of sample collection, clinical relevant anemia, clinical relevant abnormalities of the urinary tract, clinical relevant abnormalities of the mouth or the salivary glands, acute diseases, pregnant or breast-feeding women, employees of the department of Clinical Pharmacology at the Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg, students still having to take exams at the department of Clinical Pharmacology (especially students studying medicine, dentistry, molecular medicine, pharmacy or medical process management)
